requestSummary: Correct the alleged errors in five of six proposed LHD vocational standard calculations before finalization.
codingRationale: The response expressly disagrees that the NPRM contained the alleged error and says the commenter misunderstood the method. A separate collective method revision is not acceptance of this allegation.

requestSummary: Specify that vehicles without an installed propulsion engine use CI Multi-Purpose standards, rather than urban or regional standards.
codingRationale: CARB appears in the reproduced blocks but is not named in the section summary. The shared response retains CI certification while permitting appropriate urban, regional or multi-purpose categorization, contrary to the requested Multi-Purpose-only limitation. This is not coded as an explicit rejection of CARB.

organization: China WTO/TBT National Notification & Enquiry Center
requestSummary: Clarify the calculation method and sources of the proposed 2027-2032 vocational CO2 standard values in Table II-19.
codingRationale: The named response explains international comparability limits but does not reconstruct the requested proposed table or identify its input sources. The shared discussion describes a revised final method and points to the RIA; it is not treated as a verified complete answer to this distinct proposed-table question.

organization: China WTO/TBT National Notification & Enquiry Center
requestSummary: Explain whether differences between the proposed calculated standards and cited international methods or values are reasonable.
codingRationale: EPA names China WTO and explains that payload, test weight, aerodynamic assumptions and drive cycles affect numerical CO2 values. This is a qualitative comparability explanation, not a numerical reconciliation or endorsement of the comment's international-standard premise.

requestSummary: Clarify that the CO2 credit equation applies to tractors as well as vocational vehicles.
codingRationale: EPA names Cummins and confirms continued tractor credit eligibility. The proposed vocational reference was not intended to exclude tractors; this is clarification rather than newly granted eligibility.

requestSummary: Allow manufacturers to use engineering judgment to choose an appropriate ZEV regulatory subcategory based on the vehicle replaced.
codingRationale: EPA names DTNA's engineering-judgment request in its summary and describes retaining appropriate urban, regional or multi-purpose certification. Repeated request wording and cross-references within this block are collapsed. Agreement in direction is not an individual effect or proof that every requested flexibility was adopted.

requestSummary: Exempt ZEV-generated ABT credits from the averaging-set limitations in 40 CFR 1037.740.
codingRationale: The excerpt contains this distinct request in DTNA's answer to EPA request 53. Section 2.5's response does not separately resolve the averaging-set exemption. Other response sections and the original letter's referenced sections were not reviewed for this request.

requestSummary: Continue allowing ZEV credit calculation in any appropriate vocational subcategory according to intended use instead of requiring Multi-Purpose categorization.
codingRationale: EPA names PACCAR's intended-use and lead-time concerns in its summary and describes not finalizing the common-reference approach. This is shared policy-direction consistency, not an individually identified effect.

requestSummary: If EPA nevertheless requires Multi-Purpose categorization, defer implementation until at least MY2030.
codingRationale: EPA summarizes the requested delay but says it is not finalizing the common-reference approach that triggers this fallback. The section does not separately adopt MY2030. The fallback must not be counted as an unconditional delay request or a second successful reform change.

requestSummary: Re-evaluate the vocational stringency-setting procedure because common absolute reductions have different consequences across manufacturers' vehicle mixes.
codingRationale: EPA summarizes Volvo's standard-setting concern and describes changing to a tractor-like method after considering comments. The request and shared revision align in direction, without establishing that Volvo caused the revision or validating the numerical examples in the excerpt.

requestSummary: Re-evaluate the proposed requirement to categorize zero-emission vocational vehicles in CI Multi-Purpose service classes.
codingRationale: The second part of Volvo's joint request concerns categorization rather than the standard-setting calculation. EPA's shared response permits the appropriate subcategory. These two Volvo requests are not independent comments or independently attributable policy changes.
